newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy was seen intervening in morning - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy was seen intervening in morning - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Italy was seen selling marks for lira on Monday morning when the lira touched a low of 1,003.60 per mark, dealers said.

"The central bank made its presence felt all morning, checking prices for amounts greater than usual and made its first intervention around 1,003.60 which brought the lira back around 1,001 per mark," one said.
"It's in the Bank of Italy's interest "to have mark/lira below 1,000," this dealer added.
"The Bank has been giving very strong signals," another added.
At 1305 GMT, the lira was quoted at 1,001.35/1.65 per mark after touching a day's high of 999.15.
The lira returned to Europe's exchange rate mechanism at the end November with a central parity against the mark of 990.
